chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Zurara [or] Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The women do not inherit anything from the real estate of the houses, but the construction and the bricks are evaluated, and they are given one-eighth or one-quarter of its value.
He said: And that is so that the women do not get married, thereby spoiling the inheritance of the heirs.

key_terms.عَقَارِ الدُّورِ: Real estate of the houses (immovable property)

ai.seo_question: How do women inherit from real estate (houses) in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the Shia juristic distinction between inheriting the land (arad) and the structure (a'yan), where women receive a monetary valuation of the building rather than the land itself. The rationale of preventing disruption to male heirs' inheritance rights reflects the socio-legal context of maintaining family property integrity within the extended lineage. This ruling highlights the nuanced application of inheritance laws in early Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the preservation of the estate's core asset.
